name: Dong Hoi food guide
summary: Cháo canh is the everyday bowl of noodles, snakehead, and a crisp fried ram, and bánh khoái is the large crisp cake with a pork, tomato, and pineapple sauce. Khoai deo is the sun-dried sweet potato you take home from the market.
body: Start at Chợ Đồng Hới on Mẹ Suốt, beside the river. The hall sells bánh xèo, cháo canh, bánh canh, and kẹo cu đơ, mostly in the early morning and the afternoon.

Bánh khoái here is a larger crisp cake with pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts, and a sauce of pork, tomato, and pineapple. It is not the Hue crepe. The small cakes sit on Lê Thành Đồng, Cô Tám, and Đồng Hải.
specialtiesLead: Khoai deo is the sun-dried sweet to take home. The rows below are the other plates of this coast.

spots.name: Chao canh
spots.address: Chợ Đồng Hới, Lê Thành Đồng, Đồng Hải, Nguyễn Trãi, Lý Thường Kiệt
spots.note: Cháo canh is the everyday Quảng Bình bowl: soft noodles, lean pork, snakehead, and a crisp fried ram in a light broth. Some shops simmer marrow bones, some use pork rib with shrimp and fish, and some tint the broth with turmeric and add mustard greens.

spots.name: Banh khoai
spots.address: Cô Tám and Lê Thành Đồng
spots.note: A large crisp rice-batter cake, filled with seasoned pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts, eaten hot with herbs. The sauce is pork, tomato, pineapple, and peanut, with cucumber, starfruit, fig, unripe banana, and shrimp ruốc on the side.

spots.name: Banh bot loc
spots.address: Lê Thành Đồng and Đồng Hải
spots.note: A hot cassava-flour cake filled with shrimp and pork, eaten plain, steamed in a banana leaf, or fried, with mushroom and sour bamboo shoot in one account and wood-ear and mung bean in another.

spots.name: Banh mi with tapioca cakes
spots.nameVi: Bánh mì kẹp bánh bột lọc
spots.note: A hot split loaf stuffed with banana-leaf cassava cakes of shrimp and pork, plus chili threads, herbs, and a thin sweetened fish sauce. Chợ Đồng Hới also fills the same loaf with a mung-bean cake.

spots.name: Banh beo
spots.address: Lê Thành Đồng, Cô Tám, and Đồng Hải
spots.note: Đồng Hới bánh bèo is a soft rice cake, not the small Hue or Da Nang cup: it smells of new rice and carries browned shrimp in a salty-sweet fish sauce. Another account pours it thin, with some chew, and tops it with stir-fried sea shrimp and tương ớt.

spots.name: Banh nam
spots.note: Bánh nậm is rice flour steamed 15–20 minutes and wrapped in lá dong, with a shrimp filling.

spots.name: Banh cuon with shrimp ruoc
spots.note: A morning rice sheet with no filling, eaten with shrimp ruốc, thin cucumber, herbs, and nước lèo. It is not the filled Hanoi roll.

spots.name: Banh xeo
spots.note: A red-rice crepe, rolled just off the pan with snakehead, herbs, bean sprouts, lettuce, and sesame, then pinched in bánh đa. Quảng Hòa uses the same red rice with cá chuối and bánh đá, and bánh xèo Ba Đồn is a separate crepe.

spots.name: Keo cu do
spots.note: Kẹo cu đơ is the sweet at Chợ Đồng Hới, sold with the crepe and the noodle bowls, in the early morning and the afternoon.

spots.name: Den bien
spots.note: Đẻn biển is a small sea snake, also called mãng xà biển, stir-fried with lemongrass and chili, simmered as porridge, or minced and fried in rice paper as ram. One plate comes with bánh đa.

spots.name: Grilled stingray
spots.note: Stingray from the Nhật Lệ mouth, seasoned and grilled on foil or a banana leaf, then eaten hot with herbs and rice paper.

spots.name: Banh uot in Con
spots.note: Bánh ướt in Cộn is a thin rice sheet, smooth, chewy, and soft, steamed a few dozen seconds after the batter has rested a day and a night. More than 16 households in Đồng Sơn still make the sheets by hand.

spots.name: Goi ca
spots.address: Center, and boats on the Nhật Lệ
spots.note: Thin slices of grouper or cá mai, cooked in lime juice at the table and rolled in rice paper with herbs.

spots.name: Fried snails
spots.note: Apple snail and spiral snail, fried with chili, fish sauce, and pepper, then coconut, pineapple, ginger, lemongrass, and lime leaf until golden. Eat them with green-mango salad, or with a cracker dipped in the sauce.

spots.name: Bun cha ca
spots.note: A morning bowl on Lê Trực: thin noodles, a cake of cá thác lác, and a broth of fish bone or pork bone, with pickled shallot, chili, lettuce, and banana flower.

spots.name: Chao san ca loc
spots.address: Tôn Đức Thắng, Nguyễn Thái Học, Hà Huy Tập and Hoàng Diệu
spots.note: Cháo sắn cá lóc is the bowl on Tôn Đức Thắng, Nguyễn Thái Học, and the Hà Huy Tập–Hoàng Diệu corner.

spots.name: Chao hau
spots.address: Quán Hàu, about 7 km south on National Highway 1A
spots.note: Nhật Lệ oysters, stir-fried with scallion, chili, pepper, and fish sauce, then stirred into rice porridge, or dropped raw into the boiling pot. Spring, around Tết, is the full season; from July through November the oysters are fewer.

sections.heading: Beyond the market
paragraphs: These three sit on the river mouths and under the Lý Hòa pass, a ride out from the market.

spots.name: Roon River cockles
spots.address: Chợ Cảnh Dương, near the Roòn bridge, old Quảng Trạch
spots.note: Roòn River cockles, where salt and fresh water meet, steamed, grilled, or eaten raw with lime after a soak that makes them spit the sand. The other plates are cockle porridge, a tamarind sauce, and the lime plate, which is the one to order.

spots.name: Chao ca ngheo
spots.address: Đá Nhảy, under the Lý Hòa pass
spots.note: Cá nghéo is a cartilaginous fish with lean meat and rough skin. The porridge at Đá Nhảy finishes it with oyster mushroom, straw mushroom, and button mushroom, over green mustard, with Đồng Hới fish sauce and hot chili.

spots.name: Crab and winter melon
spots.note: Sea crab steamed with winter melon, a summer plate. The melon is cool and the crab is sweet.

sections.heading: Markets and eating streets
paragraphs: One hall and three eating streets.

spots.name: Dong Hoi Market
spots.caption: The hall on Mẹ Suốt, beside the river.
spots.note: An ordinary hall on Mẹ Suốt, and the walk for bánh xèo, cháo canh, bánh canh, and kẹo cu đơ. Most counters sell in the early morning and the afternoon.

spots.name: Le Thanh Dong
spots.note: Bánh bột lọc, bánh bèo, bánh khoái, and cháo canh sit on this street.

spots.name: Co Tam
spots.note: Bánh khoái and bánh bèo are the cakes on Cô Tám.

spots.name: Dong Hai
spots.note: Bánh bột lọc, bánh bèo, and cháo canh by day. After 18:00 on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, Đồng Hải is also part of the walking street.

seoTitle: Dong Hoi food guide — chao canh, banh khoai, khoai deo
seoDescription: Chao canh, banh khoai, and khoai deo in Dong Hoi, plus the small cakes and Nhat Le seafood.
